headline: A federal judge vacates the Pentagon's blacklist of Anthropic, calling it retaliation
deck: Judge Rita Lin's 59-page order finds the "supply chain risk" designation punished Anthropic for refusing to let Claude be used in autonomous weapons and mass surveillance, not for any real security concern.

headline: Nvidia is reportedly nearing a deal to buy Hugging Face, but nothing is signed
deck: The Information reported Nvidia "agreed to buy" the open-model hub for roughly $13 billion, while Business Insider says talks could still collapse; neither company has commented.

headline: Nvidia's Vera CPU starts shipping, with AWS among the first hyperscalers taking delivery
deck: Anthropic, OpenAI, Oracle Cloud and SpaceX AI received the earliest systems as AWS and Nvidia expand a 16-year partnership to include Vera CPU-based infrastructure.

headline: Google ships Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash with scene extension and 4K upscaling
deck: The video model can now extend generated scenes to 40 seconds, take specified first and last frames, and draft cheap 360p previews before a full-resolution render.

headline: DeepMind pilots a double-blind way to test its own models against secret benchmarks
deck: A cryptographic "box" built on confidential computing lets outside evaluators test a proprietary model without seeing its weights, and without Google seeing the test questions.

headline: Barret Zoph returns to Google as VP of research after a five-month stop at OpenAI
deck: The Thinking Machines Lab co-founder left Google in 2022, spent two years at OpenAI, co-founded and was pushed out of his own startup, then rejoined OpenAI before now returning to Google.

headline: Deep Cogito raises $43 million to keep pushing self-improving open models
deck: The Series A, led by TQ Ventures with Zscaler joining as both investor and customer, brings the post-training startup's total funding past $56 million.

headline: Cohere Labs releases a 2.4B vision model built to read documents at native resolution
deck: North Micro Vision skips the usual downsizing step, processing pages up to A4 size at 200dpi and scoring 0.921 on DocVQA.

headline: Stanford payroll data shows AI's hiring freeze on young workers widening, not stabilising
deck: The employment gap for 22-to-25-year-olds in AI-exposed jobs grew from 15% to 19% in a year, and the mechanism is reduced hiring, not layoffs.

headline: Bill Gates says AI has crossed every danger threshold the industry once named as a limit
deck: Three years after calling AI-driven job disruption "manageable," Gates now argues the economy, biosecurity and criminal misuse thresholds have all been passed.

headline: OpenAI's data centre chief exits in the company's 13th senior departure this year
deck: Chris Malone leaves after 16 months and a reorganisation moved him off reporting to Greg Brockman; his responsibilities now split across three separate leaders.

headline: Nvidia claims Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers 30 times the throughput per watt of its last generation
deck: The figure comes from an agentic-coding benchmark still pending independent review by SemiAnalysis, and Nvidia's own post notes it doesn't yet reflect the new CPU's tool-calling performance.

headline: Bengaluru's Ringg AI raises $10 million as it pushes voice agents past the phone call
deck: The Series A extension, led by Peak XV, brings the company's total funding to $15.5 million; it already handles 20 million call attempts a month for Cred, Flipkart and Practo.

headline: IBM ships Granite 4.2, an Apache-licensed reasoning model built for local deployment
deck: The 3B, 8B and 30B models add a thinking-mode toggle and a 512K-token context window, with the larger two trained further on agentic software-engineering tasks.

headline: Stability AI raises $76 million backed by Universal, Sony and Warner Music
deck: The round brings total funding to $232 million and includes EA and AMD Ventures, aimed at expanding creative-production tools and professional services.

headline: MiniMax revenue surges 283% but stays well short of its full-year forecast
deck: H1 revenue reached $116.6m and enterprise revenue grew 703%, yet that is only about a third of the $363.77m analysts had projected for the full year.

headline: Perplexity and Nvidia ship a local AI agent platform that bills nothing per token
deck: Portable Computer runs Qwen, Perplexity's own PPLX model and Nvidia's Nemotron on a single RTX GPU with at least 24GB of memory, escalating to cloud models only when needed.

headline: Anthropic unifies Claude's memory across chat and Cowork so context carries over
deck: Sensitive categories like health and political-belief data stay excluded by default, and government ID numbers are never stored regardless of settings.

headline: Nvidia says the same model scores 30% or 100% on ARC-AGI-3 depending on its harness
deck: Claude Opus 5 cleared all 183 levels wrapped in Nvidia's AVO system, against 30% on its own — a vendor-run result on a public benchmark, not yet independently reproduced.

headline: Amazon's business-process benchmark finds more tools make AI agents worse
deck: Success nearly halved when the six tools an agent needed were buried among twenty, and Claude 4.5 underperformed Claude 4 on reasoning-style agents.

headline: Starcloud raises $250m for orbital data centres as launch capacity tightens
deck: The round values the 25-person company at $2.3bn, with Nvidia putting in $25m — and its chief executive naming Falcon 9's 2028 retirement as the binding constraint.

headline: OpenAI-backed legal firm Harvey rebuilds its model on China's open-weight Kimi K3
deck: Harvey previously tuned closed models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google; it now post-trains Moonshot AI's open base, citing inference cost and the ability to train on legal data.

headline: China's state carriers turn spare capacity into AI compute, with one unit up 95%
deck: China Telecom's intelligent-computing revenue nearly doubled and China Unicom booked 41.9bn yuan from compute power, as the operators resell capacity as "token factories".

headline: Nvidia takes a minority stake in power-infrastructure developer Cloverleaf
deck: Several hundred million dollars into a company that sits between utilities and data centres, days after Nvidia put $1.5bn into an OpenAI-linked site in Ohio.

headline: Outer Biosciences trains a skincare model on human tissue kept alive for a month
deck: Keeping surgical skin viable for weeks rather than days lets the company observe collagen remodelling, feeding results back into a model that proposes new compounds.

headline: Nvidia moves a KV cache between models with linear regression, skipping the re-prefill
deck: Transferring a 32,768-token cache from Qwen3 14B to 32B took 278 milliseconds against seven seconds to recompute it, holding 73% to 98% of standalone accuracy.

headline: Encrypted instructions on a web page make Grok hand over a user's chat history
deck: Adversa AI reported the attack to xAI on 3 June and reproduced it again on 19 August; there is still no patch, no CVE and no workaround a user can apply.

headline: OpenAI offers to keep nothing at all for frontier-model API customers
deck: A companion system, Private Safety Processing, is meant to let automated abuse detection run across a customer's traffic without any employee seeing the prompts.

headline: Nevada clears Tesla, Waymo and Uber to run up to 8,000 robotaxis in Clark County
deck: Tesla took the largest allocation at 5,000 vehicles and then told regulators it does not expect to deploy anything close to that within the year.

headline: A third of web pages published since ChatGPT launched show signs of AI authorship
deck: Pew put the figure at 35% for pages published after November 2022, and flagged that detection tools misclassify human writing often enough to treat the number as directional.

headline: OpenAI is closing the gap with Anthropic among business buyers, card data suggests
deck: Ramp's spending data puts Anthropic ahead at about 44% to OpenAI's 40% in July, with OpenAI growing faster this quarter — on a sample that skews to tech.

headline: Bedrock adds cross-Region routing for GPT-5.6, pooling capacity across 25 regions
deck: Requests for Sol, Terra and Luna can now draw on compute outside the region they were sent to, which AWS says holds throughput steady when a single region is saturated.

headline: Google gives publishers a button that lets readers pin them in Search and Discover
deck: More than 345,000 sources have been selected since May, and Google says readers click through to a preferred source about twice as often.

headline: Micro1 says its gross run rate reached $500m, five times its level eight months ago
deck: The AI training-data supplier nets $150m to $200m of that, and says it refuses to sell to Chinese developers on national-security grounds.

headline: An AI agent ran a protein design pipeline unaided and hit 14 of 15 wet-lab targets
deck: Anthropic reports hit rates of 22.6% to 35.1% against an industry norm of 10-15%, and says the work stays restricted in its public models pending a trusted-access programme.

headline: Unitree becomes mainland China's first listed humanoid robot maker, closing up 460%
deck: The Hangzhou company raised 6.1bn yuan and rose as much as 629% intraday, on 2025 revenue of about $250m from robots still mostly used for demonstrations.

headline: Nvidia leads a $74m extension into Sarvam, India's sovereign-model startup
deck: The Bengaluru company reached unicorn status in June at a $1.5bn valuation, and the chipmaker backing it also supplies the GPUs India's sovereign AI programme runs on.

headline: Fractile seeks a $6.5bn valuation on an Anthropic chip deal and no shipping product
deck: The British startup's valuation would rise more than sixfold since May on a $250m supply agreement for inference chips that are not expected to ship until 2027.

headline: Three of 1,357 FDA-authorised AI medical devices were tested on patient outcomes
deck: A PLOS Digital Health analysis found only 34 of the cleared devices were linked to a registered clinical trial, and most studies excluded pregnant women and adults over 75.

headline: Chinese and US customers pay Samsung more than Taiwanese ones for the same nodes
deck: New July orders on the 4nm and 5nm lines cost 10-15% more for customers in China and America, against 5-10% for those in Taiwan, as TSMC's capacity fills up.

headline: China slows exports of germanium and quartz materials to Taiwan, Nikkei reports
deck: Optical and chip-equipment suppliers report prolonged customs checks with no stated reason, forcing cancelled orders and longer production lead times.

headline: SK Hynix will buy back and cancel $28.6bn of its own shares on the AI memory boom
deck: The 40 trillion won programme is the largest treasury share cancellation by a listed South Korean company, covering about 3.3% of shares outstanding.

headline: Microsoft patches a one-click Copilot data-theft flaw eight months after disclosure
deck: The bug let a single malicious link pull data from a victim's connected Gmail, Drive and Calendar — and Copilot itself revealed the undocumented parameter that made it work.

headline: Grok 4.6 reaches Amazon Bedrock with a 500K context window and tiered pricing
deck: The model shipped on August 12; what is new is enterprise availability through AWS and a price that doubles once a prompt passes 200,000 tokens.

headline: Google gives US college students a free year of AI Pro and adds a study hub
deck: The offer covers a $19.99-a-month plan, with students outside the US getting the cheaper AI Plus tier and 400GB of storage instead.

headline: Anthropic raises its own misalignment risk rating and keeps a stronger model unreleased
deck: The company says the change reflects rising uncertainty about its evaluations, not new evidence that either its released or unreleased systems are more dangerous.

headline: Pennsylvania requires local approval before the state will permit new AI data centers
deck: Executive Order 2026-05 also bars nondisclosure agreements on data center deals and strips fast-track permitting from a governor who once championed the buildout.

headline: Microsoft's installed AI chip count falls well short of its $280bn buildout, investigation finds
deck: A Guardian investigation puts Microsoft's installed AI chips at 2.2 million against $280bn in spending since 2022, a gap Nadella blames on power and building delays.

headline: Anthropic seeks a credit facility topping $10 billion ahead of a possible fall IPO
deck: The revolving credit line would be four times the $2.5 billion facility Anthropic arranged last year, with lead banks asked to commit roughly $1.25 billion each.

headline: OpenAI rolls out a separate ChatGPT for teens with age detection and parental controls
deck: The 13-to-17 experience routes suspected minors in automatically, strips romantic language from responses, and lets parents set quiet hours, though not read conversations.

headline: Cerebras unveils a CS-4 chip it says is 30 times faster than GPUs at inference
deck: The company's own benchmark leans on sparsity and a doubled clock speed rather than a new chip design, and its peak bandwidth figure is untested in practice, an independent analysis found.

headline: Most Americans now say they're more concerned than excited about AI, Pew finds
deck: The share of adults under 30 who feel more wary than enthusiastic about AI has grown from 39% to 55% in two years, according to a new Pew Research Center survey.

headline: DOJ investigates Andreessen Horowitz over two partners' rival board seats
deck: A year-old Justice Department probe centers on Ben Horowitz's Databricks seat and Martin Casado's Fivetran seat, after the two AI data companies became direct competitors.

headline: CISA orders federal agencies to patch a critical flaw in the Ray AI framework
deck: The code-injection vulnerability, actively exploited via a browser-based attack, carries a 9.4 CVSS score and a three-day federal remediation deadline.

headline: Google shuts down its Imagen 4 API endpoints, pushing developers to Gemini
deck: The three Imagen 4 generation endpoints stopped working August 17, and Google directs developers to its Gemini-native image models as the replacement path.

headline: AI accounting startup Rillet raises $100 million, reaching a $1 billion valuation
deck: The Series C, led by ICONIQ with Sequoia, Andreessen Horowitz and six other investors, is Rillet's third fundraise in a year and pushes total funding past $200 million.

headline: Palona AI raises $20 million to bring AI automation to restaurants and retail
deck: The Series A, led by Ardenwood Ventures, funds a vision-AI platform already deployed at chains including Cali BBQ to monitor operations and coordinate frontline teams.

headline: Nvidia guarantees $105bn and takes a $1.5bn stake to lock up an Ohio site for OpenAI
deck: The chipmaker becomes the exclusive compute supplier at a Pike County campus OpenAI has leased for 20 years, extending a financing pattern that has drawn scrutiny for funding Nvidia's own biggest customer.

headline: Anthropic's revenue run rate passes $65bn, overtaking OpenAI ahead of a possible IPO
deck: The figure, shared with investors and first reported by Bloomberg, is up from $47bn in May — a pace that puts Anthropic ahead of OpenAI's reported $40bn as both companies prepare confidential listing paperwork.

headline: Groq raises $350m at a $3.5bn valuation, half its peak, to fund its cloud pivot
deck: The round, led by Disruptive with Nvidia expected to join, is Groq's second since it licensed its chip technology to Nvidia for $20bn and lost its founder — at half the valuation it fetched a year ago.

headline: Stripe is reported to be buying OpenRouter for more than $7bn, five times its May valuation
deck: The model-routing gateway raised at $1.3bn three months ago. Stripe has declined to comment, and the price has not been confirmed by either company.

headline: Z.ai holds back GLM-5.3's open weights after its cyber capability outgrew its training
deck: The Beijing lab says post-training pushed the model's vulnerability-finding ability further than planned, so it is delaying the open-weights release while pairing the launch with a free security-auditing program.

headline: OpenAI's cyber-defense models reach Amazon Bedrock, restricted to vetted customers
deck: Daybreak Red and Daybreak Blue, built for vulnerability research and incident response, require enrollment in OpenAI's own screening program before an AWS customer can request access.

headline: Researchers show weak, unnoticed prompt cues can be combined to strongly steer AI models
deck: The technique, which the authors call "model hypnosis," works across model families and sizes and transfers between models, complicating both AI safety review and interpretability work.

headline: Most young Americans say they don't trust any major AI company's CEO, CNBC poll finds
deck: In a survey of 1,088 people aged 18 to 34, Palantir's Alex Karp scored worst at 81% distrust and Microsoft's Satya Nadella scored best — and still ended up net-distrusted.

headline: Firebird opens the CIS region's largest AI data center in Armenia, built in six months
deck: The site is planned to host more than 70,000 Nvidia Rubin and Blackwell GPUs and scale to 300 megawatts, with Armenia's prime minister among the officials at the opening.

headline: xAI ships Grok 4.6, matching GPT-5.6 Sol on Artificial Analysis's intelligence index
deck: The update keeps Grok 4.5's base model and 500,000-token context, spending the gains on longer training for agentic and knowledge-work tasks rather than a larger model.

headline: Nvidia hands the AI build-out to Wall Street with a $500bn financing push
deck: Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR will raise third-party capital for data centres, with Nvidia backstopping part of the value of the chips pledged as collateral.

headline: OpenAI pauses work on Astra after tests flag possible critical cyber capability
deck: The company says it cannot rule out that an unreleased model crosses its Preparedness Framework threshold for cybersecurity, and has halted internal work that does not meet new controls.

headline: Cognition is in talks to raise at $40bn, three months after a $26bn round
deck: Bloomberg reports the coding company is fielding early investor interest at a valuation more than half again its May mark, on annualised revenue said to be approaching $1bn.

headline: The EU's transparency rules for AI-generated content are now being enforced
deck: Chatbots must identify themselves, deepfakes must be labelled, and synthetic content must carry machine-readable marks, with the Commission's AI Office enforcing from 2 August.

headline: Nvidia aims Nemotron 3.5 Lightning at agent workloads with a 30B sparse model
deck: The company claims up to four times the output speed of comparable models, and pairs the release with Switchyard, an open router that sends each step of a workflow to a different model.

headline: Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B lands under Apache 2.0 with a 262,144-token context
deck: The model card lists a vision encoder, a hybrid Gated DeltaNet and attention stack across 64 layers, and coding scores of 73.0 on Terminal Bench and 61.7 on SWE-bench Pro.

headline: Google's Gemini 3.7 Flash undercuts its own predecessor by half on price
deck: The workhorse model posts 65.3% on DeepSWE v1.1 against 49.0% for 3.6 Flash, and runs at $0.75 per million input tokens until the end of the year.

headline: DeepSeek publishes V4-Pro under an MIT licence at 1.7 trillion parameters
deck: The model card reports 87.9 on Terminal Bench 2.1 and 83.3 on Cybergym, and ships with three selectable reasoning effort levels.

headline: Anthropic publishes a technical account of how Claude's text watermark works
deck: The post appeared on 14 August, twelve days after EU rules began requiring machine-readable marks on AI-generated content shown to European users.

headline: Nvidia makes the case for treating GPU capacity as infrastructure debt
deck: Published a day after the financing announcement, the post argues that compute should be underwritten the way toll roads and power plants are.

headline: Nvidia makes the case for 800-volt DC power architecture in AI factories
deck: The company argues that scaling compute performance now requires changing how power is distributed inside the data centre, not only how the chips are cooled.

headline: Nvidia courts the local AI community around open models and agents
deck: The post accompanies the Nemotron releases and is aimed at developers running models on their own hardware rather than through a hosted API.

headline: Indonesia opens its first university AI centre, with Indosat and Nvidia
deck: Universitas Gadjah Mada is the host institution, in a partnership framed around developing local AI talent rather than exporting compute capacity.
